slides.title: [Parent] / document / retriever
slides.hook: The top 4 chunks all missed the answer. Return the section around the top hit, and size that section yourself.
inside: A real run where the parent held the answer

slides.title: Match [small], / return the section
slides.text: Small chunks give sharp embeddings but little context. LangChain's `ParentDocumentRetriever` (in `langchain-classic`) keeps both:

steps: `parent_splitter` cuts each document into parents, such as sections.
`child_splitter` cuts each parent into small children.
Each child is embedded with its parent's id in `doc_id`.
Parents go into a docstore under that id.
A query finds the top `k` children, keeps their unique parent ids in rank order and returns those parents.

slides.title: The parent held / the [answer]
slides.text: A 4-section support handbook, 23 children of up to 100 characters. Query: "How long do warranty repairs take?"

visuals.label: Top 4 children (spaCy en_core_web_md vectors)

chunks.text: The warranty covers manufacturing faults. It does not cover water damage or drops.
Warranty claims need the serial number. Approved claims get a repair or a replacement.
Damaged parcels are replaced at no cost when the customer sends a photo within 7 days.
Refunds go back to the original payment method.

visuals.verdict: The answer sentence ranked outside the top 4

visuals.label: Parent returned first: Warranty, 347 characters
chunks: ## Warranty … Approved claims get a repair or a replacement. !!Repairs take about 10 business days.!! …
visuals.verdict: The answer comes back with the parent

slides.title: No parent splitter: / the whole [document]
slides.text: `parent_splitter` defaults to `None`. Then the parent is the raw document you passed in. Same handbook, same 23 children:

options.output: !!1 parent, 1,360 characters!!: the whole handbook for every query
4 parents: 401, 354, 347 and 251 characters, one per section

slides.after: Load a 200-page PDF as one document and every hit returns all 200 pages. Split parents on headings first.

slides.title: `k` counts / [children]
slides.text: `search_kwargs` is empty by default, so the vector store's `k=4` applies to children. Parents are then deduped. The warranty query:
slides.after: The query "Who has to approve refunds over $500?" returns 2 parents at k=4. Budget for k × your largest parent, then set `k` in `search_kwargs`.

slides.title: Re-ingest [doubles] / every parent
slides.text: `add_documents` gives each parent a new random id (`uuid4`). The same handbook, added twice:

visuals.code:
children          23 → 46
parents            4 → 8
top 4 children    {{2 Warranty, each twice}}
returned          Warranty ×2 (two ids)

bullets: The retriever has no delete method. Remove old children from the vector store and old parents from the docstore yourself.
Passing `ids` with a `parent_splitter` fails unless there's one id per parent after splitting.

slides.title: In-memory parents / [vanish]
slides.text: With `InMemoryStore`, the docstore in the docs' example, parents live in the Python process. A new process, same vector store:
bullets: No error: missing parents are filtered out and you get an empty list.
Pass a persistent `byte_store`, such as `LocalFileStore`, or a database-backed store.

slides.title: [Scores] stay / behind
slides.text: Parents come back with the parent's own metadata: no similarity score and no record of which child matched.
bullets: To cite the matching line, run `similarity_search_with_score` on the children yourself.
The retriever's `similarity_score_threshold` mode drops weak hits, but needs relevance scores; `InMemoryVectorStore` raises `NotImplementedError`.

slides.title: LlamaIndex merges / by [ratio]
slides.text: LlamaIndex's `AutoMergingRetriever` swaps in a parent only when more than half of its children are retrieved.

visuals.label: Defaults in llama-index-core 0.14.25
visuals.code:
AutoMergingRetriever(
    vector_retriever, storage_context,
    simple_ratio_thresh={{0.5}})
HierarchicalNodeParser.from_defaults()
# chunk_sizes=[2048, 512, 128]

bullets: One matching child out of four comes back on its own.
LangChain's retriever returns the parent on a single hit.

slides.title: Put it all / [together]
slides.text: Section-sized parents, small children, a set `k` and a docstore that survives a restart:

visuals.code:
parent = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=2000,
    separators=["\n## ", "\n\n", "\n",
                ". ", " "])
child = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=400)
retriever = ParentDocumentRetriever(
    vectorstore=vectorstore,
    byte_store=LocalFileStore("./parents"),
    child_splitter=child,
    parent_splitter=parent,
    search_kwargs={"k": 4})

bullets: LangChain's own example uses 2000 and 400 characters. Check k × 2000 characters against your token budget.
On re-ingest, delete the old children and parents first.

cards.title: Use it when
items: Answers need the whole section: steps, conditions, exceptions
Documents have headings to cut parents on
k × your largest parent fits the context budget

cards.title: Move on when
items: Sections are long and the answer sits in a sentence or two: try sentence-window retrieval
Sections run to thousands of tokens
You need scores or the matched line for citations

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: Embed small children, return their parent section
Re-adding duplicates: delete old copies first
Persist the docstore, or a restart returns []

slides.line: Go smaller still: embed single sentences, then hand the model the sentences around each hit.
